final_answer.conclusion: Completed-order value increased because completed-order count growth more than offset the decline in average completed-order value.
final_answer.recommended_next_step: Investigate what drove the completed-order count increase and whether it is sustainable, while keeping lower average completed-order value visible as a secondary investigation.
supporting_facts: Completed-order count increased 33.03% from October to December.
Completed-order value increased 18.68% from October to December.
Average completed-order value decreased 10.79% from October to December.
final_answer.important_limitation: This descriptive analysis does not establish why either metric changed.

methodology.population: Orders with status exactly completed and order_date from 2024-10-01 inclusive to 2025-01-01 exclusive.
methodology.calculation_summary: Group completed orders by calendar month, count rows, sum total_amount, calculate average total_amount, and compare October with December.
validation_checks: Confirmed one row per order_id in the source table.
Reconciled monthly results with quarter totals.
Repeated the calculation with an independent conditional aggregation.
assumptions: order_date is the governing date for the review.
total_amount is completed-order value and is not labeled revenue.
